en: Preface to the Reprinted Ritual for Repentance at the Nianfo Hall In observing those throughout ancient and modern times who have discussed the practice of nianfo for rebirth in the Pure Land, I find that many boast of their own power.

Their arguments typically include such claims as "the mind-only pure land is reached without going" or "the self-nature Amitābha is realized without being accomplished. I humbly believe that these theories seem— (Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly. The translation reflects the portion available.)
This is to slight the power of the Buddha. Now, as for the Buddha, his essence is luminous and pure, such that there is nothing obscure he does not illuminate.
There may be someone who, though they do not know why the Buddha is called "Buddha," merely follows the words of others and recites "Namo Buddha.

Such a person has already, within the Tathāgata’s wondrous wisdom of observation, accomplished the direct cause for the stage of Buddhahood—this is what is meant by being born from a lotus in the Jasper Pond.
It is like a wandering fish swallowing a hook; though it does not know that the hook is what makes it a hook, once the fish has entered the hand of the one holding the hook, it is lost.
Thus we know that the single word "Buddha" is but a single hook within the ocean of awakening.
The Tripitaka Master Hyeon of Goryeo, who resided at Daecheong Yeonsungsa Temple in Daebuyu, had long kept this essential teaching hidden within himself.

Coincidentally, while examining the *Mida Ch’an-bop* (Amitābha Repentance Method) composed by Prince Seong of the Jin dynasty, he found that its methods for inspiring and guiding others were in perfect accord with his own mind of universal salvation.
He then contributed his own resources and entrusted the task to his fellow monk, Chupo.
He solicited contributions from all quarters and assembled craftsmen to carve the woodblocks so that it might be transmitted to distant lands, requesting me to compose a preface for it. I said:

"This is truly unprecedented! The Buddha possesses eighty-four thousand marks and signs of excellence, with radiance that shines throughout the worlds of the ten directions, embracing and never forsaking those sentient beings who practice mindfulness of the Buddha.
How much more so does our Master Tripitaka, through the *prajñā* of words and letters, embrace [all beings]!"
It gathers in sentient beings; its radiance extends through ten thousand ages in grandeur, causing all who see it and hear it to ascend together to the stage of non-retrogression.
May it eternally bless the Sage’s adamantine realm of immeasurable life. This may truly be called one hook cast down from the ocean of awakening.
Dated the [blank] day of the seventh month in the third year of the Zhishun era.
Preface by the Japanese Monk Jidō, Abbot of Daikaku-ji,
on the Amitābha Repentance and Praise,
composed by Zhao Bingwen, Grand Officer of the Household, Editor of the Hanlin Academy, and Concurrent Director of the Bureau of Edicts.
The Layman Jile (Ji-le) Wang Qingzhi compiled this text on the causes and conditions of the Pure Land as a liturgy for repentance.
The Layman Xianxian bowed his head in praise and said: "How unprecedented! In the past, there was a high official who was very close friends with a man of the Way.

Someone once exhorted him, saying: 'Sir, you are exceptionally intelligent and outstanding; why have you come to engage in such trivial and mundane matters? The official declined, saying he lacked the wit [to do so]. The exhortation continued:

The more they exerted themselves, the more the Duke said: "If you truly consider me to be exceptionally intelligent and discerning, yet still serve that [sect], there must certainly be some substance to my words.
The various sutras praise Amitābha’s Pure Land in no uncertain terms;
throughout the generations, the number of eminent scholars who have taken refuge therein has been vast. One may thus be free from doubt. As for Taibai, Le-tian, and Dong-po—"
Throughout the mountains and valleys, all know how to revere and follow [this teaching]. Can this not be called being exceptionally intelligent and penetrating?

Those who have planted roots of goodness in past lives will understand it without waiting for my words. Otherwise, one might as well be like a child watching a play, merely laughing along with the elders.
If even that is not yet the case, simply observing this repentance will yield more than half the benefit. Thus, I respectfully offer this eulogy:
Sentient beings see the Buddha, yet it is merely a single mind. The Buddha delivers sentient beings without departing from his great vows;
the mind is like a mirror, reflecting and interpenetrating one another, while the vows are like the earth, where whatever seed is planted immediately sprouts. You should observe this for yourself.
Just as great magicians, using a sun-crystal to draw forth the sun and a moon-lens to receive the moon—
though these have no coming or going, they appear due to conditions— so too should one know that the Pure Land is likewise.
It is also like two people who leave a gate and walk away from each other in opposite directions.
One person departs for Yan, another departs for Yue; they may go on until the end of their lives without ever meeting.
Yet if they were to seek one another, ten thousand *li* would be but a few inches.
Thus, the Buddha loves all sentient beings as a mother yearns for her child, even if that child has fled far away.
Though you remember this, what is the use? If you, my son, think of your mother, you will certainly see her.
I contemplate Amitābha as my compassionate mother;
as the eldest son of the Buddha, all bodhisattvas are my kinsmen.
Immeasurable wealth of Dharma is available to satisfy all desires at will;

what wise person would willingly endure the suffering of poverty, abandoning the Land of Ultimate Bliss to long for Jambudvīpa and resolve to return home? One must know the path—O Resident of Ultimate Bliss!
He is your guide; you should know that this confession is complete with all the necessary provisions.
Bowing my head to the One of Ten Powers, may he bear witness for me. O Son of the Buddha, I respectfully inform you:
you should cultivate this contemplation.
Preface to the Amitābha Repentance Ritual,
composed by Li Chunfu, Court Gentleman of the Academy of Hanlin, Attendant at the Hanlin, Concurrently Acting Director of the Bureau of Edicts,
Adjunct Secretary to the Literary Office of the Prince of Kui, Knight of the Mounted Cavalry, and Recipient of the Scarlet Fish-Bag.
Within heaven and earth, all beings possessing blood and breath harbor a fighting spirit and devour one another; their suffering is immeasurable.

Even those fortunate enough to be born as humans, who are somewhat closer to happiness, dwell in remote barbarian regions where they likewise slaughter and harm each other, remaining consistent with their state of suffering.

Furthermore, it is fortunate that one is born in the Middle Kingdom; its pleasures are quite superior. If we examine ancient histories, we find that the conditions of warfare, famine, and pestilence were characterized by a predominance of suffering.
Moreover, it is fortunate to reach old age during a well-governed era, which is truly a source of joy.
Yet, even among those who are impoverished, lowly, exhausted, or infirm, there are still many who cannot overcome their misery. As for those who possess the great fortune of being wealthy and noble—
As for those who are noble, healthy, strong, and wise—how could their joy be anything less than such?
Yet, when their desires remain unfulfilled or when calamities suddenly befall them, they still cannot avoid sorrowful reflection and lamentation; some even consider themselves to be suffering.
Thus, the Buddha’s teaching that the world of sentient beings is a realm of suffering is indeed a word of truth. Therefore, one who studies the Buddha must first...
They practiced asceticism for incalculable kalpas, seeking the bliss of nirvana, yet had not attained even a small portion of it.
How then could they swiftly transcend this suffering and calamity and proceed directly to the land of bliss? Out of great compassion, the Buddha opened the gate of skillful means and said:
"To the west lies the Land of Ultimate Bliss, where the Buddha of Infinite Life resides. If sentient beings give rise to a single thought of faith and hold fast to that Buddha..."
Upon merely hearing the name, one attains rebirth there; equal to Amitāyus, one is thereafter free from old age, illness, and death.

One’s supernatural powers and wisdom become identical to those of practitioners who have cultivated for countless kalpas, without any difference. Therefore, it is named "Ultimate Bliss" (Sukhāvatī). This is also a word of truth.
Since the Buddha's teaching traveled eastward, those who have practiced in secret and attained realization are beyond counting; yet, the ignorant do not know this.
I have recently read the *Xifang jingtu chanwen famen* (The Dharma Gate of the Repentance Text for the Western Pure Land) compiled by the Layman Jile.

It is a shortcut for those who study the Buddha’s teachings; thus, I offer my praise and record this with words of truth. Preface on the full moon day of the middle spring in the second year of the Chongqing era.
The Repentance Method of the Enabling-Operation Amitābha Dharma-Assembly:
With single-minded devotion, we take refuge in all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
Homage to the past Buddha Vipaśyin.
Homage to Śikhin Buddha.
Homage to Viśvabhū Buddha.
Homage to Krakucchanda Buddha.
Homage to the Buddha Kanakamuni.
Homage to the Buddha Kāśyapa.
Homage to the Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Homage to the Honored Maitreya Buddha of the Future.
The First Fascicle of the Ritual for Repentance at the Altar of Contemplation of Amitābha.
Compiled and Prefaced by the Layman Wang Zicheng of Jile:

In establishing this *Maitreya Amitābha Repentance Method*, I have considered that if it were extensive, its text might become overly cumbersome; yet if it were concise, its meaning might be deficient. For those who perform the regular rites of recitation and mindfulness as they arise, they need only read the large characters. However, if one seeks to investigate the fundamental causes and conditions, one must consult the small annotations.
Thus, both the extensive and the concise are preserved, benefiting both oneself and others. This entire collection consists of ten scrolls, and all subsequent volumes shall follow this model.
Originally, the Great Awakened One Śākyamuni issued his compassionate intent, earnestly praising that Amitābha;
moving with a heart of compassion, he extensively proclaimed forty-eight vows, vowing in each to deliver sentient beings, and opened sixteen gates of contemplation.
He gathers and transforms beings through every gate; he is a swift vessel for rescuing those drowning in the ocean of suffering. He guides the lost along the shortcut to escape saṃsāra.
Transcending the three realms and far surpassing the four currents, he welcomes all sentient beings from the ten directions and protects those of the nine grades as if they were his only child.
Furthermore, it is heard that throughout past and present, virtuous men and women—both monastics and laypeople—have experienced numerous such spiritual responses.
Rebirth in the Pure Land is not for just one person. Those with square faces and rounded heads should emulate the lofty spirit of Huiyuan;

those wearing scholar’s shoes and Daoist caps may admire the elegant model of the "Leftovers" (the *yimin*). When Qifang opened his heart like jade, at the end of his life, a Buddha came to welcome him back;

when Zhang Kang and Wu Qiong reached the end of their lives, the Golden Immortal led them away. Even Shanhe, who possessed the profession of a butcher, still went to the Jade Pond; as for Zhong... [text fragment ends]
Raising up the grievance of one who has been harmed and whose life was taken, he is likewise born in the Land of Gold; where the light of his compassion shines, the hells collapse and crumble.
When he upholds the holy name, the celestial Māras are struck with terror. Such is the inconceivable power of the Buddha and his unimpeded supernormal faculties.
A single utterance extinguishes the transgressions of eighty billion kalpas; a single thought attains the merit of eighty billion kalpas.
For this reason, the World-Honored One, observing the convergence of conditions in that direction for the sentient beings of this realm, has specifically opened the single gate of rebirth there.
He taught the entry into the *nien-fo* samādhi. By practicing even a brief moment of minor goodness daily, one accumulates provisions for ten thousand kalpas in the future.
In this present life, pure karma suddenly increases and adverse conditions gradually subside; humans revere them and spirits protect them, misfortunes depart and blessings arrive.
The daughter of the Li family had been blind but regained her sight; Lady Feng suffered from physical illness but was restored to health. —Shao Xiwen.
One may transcend hardships through a divine journey; Liu Huizhong experienced a nightmare yet remained unalarmed. These are the effects manifest while still in the body.
At the time of death, one is spared from descending to the Yellow Springs and shall have no further dark karma. If the process is slow, it lasts from one day up to seven days;
if rapid, it occurs from ten recitations down to a single one. One beholds the white jade-hair mark face-to-face and mounts the purple-gold throne. King Yama will not—
When summoned, transformation-buddhas come in person to welcome them, leading them directly back to the land of Ultimate Bliss and forever parting from the path of the dark underworld.
When the nun Fan beheld the sacred image outside her door, and when Tanjian obtained a lotus flower within his vase;

when celestial music filled the sky for King Udayana, and extraordinary fragrances pervaded the air for the Empress of the Sui Dynasty—these were all signs of rebirth in the Pure Land. Once one has passed away, this is called...
Removed from the registers of ghosts, they rank among the stages of Buddhahood. Auspicious signs appear at their graves as their skeletal remains radiate as *śarīra*.

Casting off the brief light of Jambudvīpa, they dwell for long ages in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*Sukhāvatī*). Born by transformation within the lotus blossoms, they take form amidst the flowers;

within the ponds of *rājīvaka* lotuses, Avalokiteśvara and Samantabhadra serve as their noble friends, while Aśvaghoṣa and Nāgārjuna become their companions in the Dharma. Though their names have passed away—
Those born as ordinary beings thus become non-retrogressive sons of the Buddha. Formerly, Shan Dao of the Tang dynasty delivered his teachings within the Wuyun Hall;
later, Tanluan of the Northern Wei manifested his form within a seven-jeweled boat. These are verifications from after death.

As the accounts of spiritual responses at the moment of passing away are extensive, I have briefly presented these auspicious signs from both before and after life; the full texts are omitted here for brevity.

The minds of ordinary beings are weak; thus, relying on one's own power, accomplishment is difficult. The vows of the Dharma-treasury are powerful; by relying on the majesty of others, success is easily achieved.

Thus, the dual benefit of self and others is realized, and compassion and wisdom are both perfected. It is fortunate that we now live in the age of the Final Dharma, at a time when this teaching is being widely propagated.

Now, this fool shall venture his limited perspective and exert his feeble pen to follow, in broad outline, the ritual protocols of Emperor Wu of Liang’s repentance liturgy and to briefly expound upon the merits of the teachings of Amitābha.

The thousand Buddhas are fully arrayed and the multitude of sages are completely revealed; the World-Honored Ones of the ten directions join their efforts to eliminate calamities, and the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time collectively provide the conditions for repenting transgressions.
They strip away the terrors of the Avīci Hell and proclaim the purity of the Land of Bliss.

Adorned with splendor, may you teach every soul on the paths of the three miserable realms to turn back their steps; at the edge of the nine-grade lotus pond, may you cause every person to advance further.
To circulate these ten scrolls of the Repentance Dharma is to deliver all sentient beings of the three periods of time. As the Sūtra says: "In the language of India, Amitābha;
in this language, it means 'Immeasurable Life,' or 'Immeasurable Light. In the language of India, Sukhāvatī; in this language, it means 'Land of Ultimate Bliss. Or...
It is called the Land of Peace and Bliss. If one upholds, maintains, reads, and recites it for those of the past, they shall be rescued from the evil realms.
For those of the present, it increases merit and dispels calamities. For those of the future, it teaches the cultivation of the Pure Land.

Extending throughout the triple world and reaching all four modes of birth, even if one has committed the ten non-virtuous actions, upon seeing or hearing [this teaching], they shall dissipate like mist. If one has transgressed the five deeds of immediate retribution, through prostrating and mindful recollection, they shall vanish like clouds.

It is extinguished. It draws in all sentient beings through transformation-birth, delivering immeasurable multitudes to attain Buddhahood. By the power of this repentance, they receive the grace of that Buddha.
Translated once for the Pure Land of the West, one attains rebirth in supreme Bodhi. Entrusting it with both hands, I pray for majestic protection, as expressed in these verses:

I have compiled this liturgy for the worship, recitation, and repentance of Amitābha, desiring to rescue all sentient beings in this turbid world so that they may together transcend the three realms and escape the cycle of saṃsāra.
May I cause them all to leave suffering behind and be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Yet, my own merit and blessings are meager and my wisdom shallow; as an ordinary and ignorant person, my learning is scant and my literary skills are crude and neglected.
I manifest the Pure Land and praise Amitābha; I take up soil to nourish mountains and use a conch-shell to measure the ocean.
My repentance methods are vast while my talent is slight; I fear and am ashamed that they do not accord with the hearts of all Buddhas.
Now, with body, speech, and mind purified, I burn incense and offer a sorrowful plea within this place of practice.
I look up and address the Three Jewels of the three periods and the ten directions, and the Amitābha Pure Land:
May you not forsake your great compassion; May your supernatural powers and the force of the Dharma secretly grant protection.
I pray that you bestow upon me the ambrosial eloquence of Avalokiteśvara, So that my writing may fill entire scrolls like that of Zhi-jue.
Above, it accords with all the sages; below, it accords with the capacities of beings.
Compiled as a method of repentance, it delivers sentient beings who see or hear it, causing them to joyfully believe and accept it.
May it circulate and spread throughout the ten directions, universally delivering the realms of all sentient beings, remaining eternally inexhaustible until the end of the future.
If there are those with the ten evil deeds or the crimes of immediate retribution, Upon encountering this method of repentance, they shall be extinguished without remainder.
Those in the present life will all possess the five spiritual powers, And those of the past will all receive the eight liberations.
At the time of death, may they all aspire to go to the Western Land, Together beholding Amitābha’s attainment of the Buddha-way.

I respectfully invoke the Triple Gem, the great assembly of the hidden and the manifest at this day’s *dharmapūjā* site: the Honored One of the three bodies and four wisdoms, perfectly luminous and endowed with the ten titles;

the subtle and wondrous teaching of the one truth contained within the eight *piṭakas* and five vehicles; the Bodhisattvas whose compassion and wisdom are both increased; and those in training and beyond training...
To the Arhats who have realized the truth; to the dragons and devas throughout the entire Dharma-realm; and to all the worthy and holy ones filling the void of space:

we humbly entreat you not to abandon your vows of compassion, but to deign to extend your discerning gaze upon us. This evening (or this morning), we establish a Pure Land ritual arena to demonstrate the path of refuge for all living beings.

We present this sublime assembly and manifest our sincere devotion. It is for the sake of [Name] and others (*[Name]—each participant should here state their own name; subsequent instances follow this pattern*).
Cycling through the three realms to receive bodies, how could one ever escape the six destinies? Like a single cloud drifting upon its substance, one has not yet emerged from the four modes of birth;

in the human realm, the eight sufferings burn together, and in the heavens, the five signs of decline cause universal distress. Were it not for the Great Compassionate Father, [there would be no salvation].
Who shall open the gate of true liberation? Those who wish to cultivate the nine grades of true refuge must repent for the evil karma of many lifetimes.
This is especially so because the perfectly luminous and wondrous essence is fundamentally but one mind; yet this illusory and fleeting life has falsely produced manifold transgressions.
These sins arise solely from delusion and are formed through association with adverse conditions; they are removed by the truth and extinguished by means of wholesome thoughts. I earnestly hope that—
May the great assembly of fellow practitioners each withdraw their divergent thoughts and attachments, completely emerge from the wheel of suffering, and together be reborn in the Land of Bliss.
Now, relying upon the Dharma-gate of Repentance according to the Bequeathed Teachings of Śākyamuni, we invoke the sages and worthies; may they deign to descend in response to our invocation.

Homage! With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite Śākyamuni Buddha, who manifests a thousand million transformation bodies, whose presence endures upon Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa and beneath the śāla trees. Homage!
With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite Amitābha Buddha, whose light shines universally, whose lifespan is inconceivable, and who made the forty-eight vows.

Homage to the Buddha Maitreya, who dwells in Tuṣita for one lifetime, who will appear at the three assemblies under the Dragon-Flower tree, and who shall descend to be born in the future. I single-mindedly entreat you to come.
Homage! With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite the Holy Lord of Five Peaks, the Seventh Patriarch and Teacher of Buddhas, the Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
Homage! With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite the Eldest Son of the Tathāgata, the King of Vows of the Dharma Realm, the Great Sage Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Homage! With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite the Great Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, whose vow-power is profoundly deep and who manifests through the Universal Gate.
Homage!
With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite the Great Holy Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva, who gathers and transforms sentient beings through the Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha.
Homage!
With single-minded devotion, we reverently invite the Bodhisattvas of the Great and Vast Wisdom, the Profound and Pure Ocean-like Multitude.
Homage; with single-minded devotion, we reverently invite all Buddhas throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions (one prostration).
Homage; with single-minded devotion, we reverently invite all Honored Dharmas throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions (one prostration).
Homage; with single-minded devotion, we reverently invite all worthy sages throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions (one prostration).
Furthermore, with single-minded devotion, I reverently invite all the Triple Gem and immeasurable worthies and sages throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions (one prostration).
Today, the great assembly of the profound and the manifest at this site of practice has already invited the Triple Gem; I now offer my utmost sincerity and lay bare my accumulated transgressions.
We pray for the merit of this rite of repentance. (Name), etc., with a sincere mind take refuge in Amitābha Buddha of the Western Pure Land, the World of Ultimate Bliss.
We take refuge in the Three Jewels of the West. First: Resolving Doubts and Generating Faith. Second: [The Practice of Contemplation].

Chapter Nine: Cultivating Practices for the Sake of Birth [in the Pure Land] Chapter Ten:

Entrustment and Circulation of the Text
○ First: Taking Refuge in the Triple Gem of the Western Quarter Now, as for taking refuge in the Triple Gem of the Western Quarter:

our Buddha, in accordance with the capacities of beings, bestows the Way; manifesting forms in response to things, he extensively expounds the Sūtras and especially praises the Land of Amitābha. When causes and conditions coincide, the Way responds in communion. If ordinary minds single-mindedly contemplate the West, the True Body will certainly descend upon Jambudvīpa.

This is like Ye Gong’s painted dragon appearing when the dragon spirit saw it, or Prince Jin’s phoenix arriving when he blew his flute; it is because the mundane and the sacred communicate through the hidden convergence of sincere resolve. Therefore:

Ci’en first proclaimed the ten excellences; Zhizhe clearly resolved the ten doubts; Li Bai and Su Zhan both spoke verses encouraging rebirth; and Prince Yuele composed a text on the vow to go [to the Pure Land]. The single blooming of the udumbara flower occurs only once in countless kalpas;

the meeting of the floating wood with the tree hole is rarer than a thousand lifetimes. The benefit gained is immense while the effort required is extremely slight. For this reason, the six directions praise it in unison and the ten lands proclaim it together. Its Master’s supreme vows are powerful, its conditions are profound, and its compassion is weighty.
If you wish to know the path for seeking rebirth in the Pure Land, you should enter the gate of Maitreya’s ritual repentance.
Today, all members of this assembly gathered at the site of practice should each collect their minds and listen attentively.

Out of compassion for all sentient beings whose hearts are shrouded by ignorance and who are deluded regarding the Pure Land—clinging to the three realms and failing to seek rebirth there—I shall now speak.
For the sake of these deluded and faithless ordinary beings who drift through birth and death within the cycle of the six realms,

I have compiled various sutras and treatises to teach the dharma-gate of repentance and ritual worship for the practice of rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, the site for delivering sentient beings.
Truly, as ordinary beings, our defilements are heavy; we are deluded by craving and indulge in committing transgressions at will. We do not fear the suffering of the hells for long kalpas.
Throughout our lives, we have been negligent, indulging only in luxury and failing to know how to cultivate spiritual progress. Only when pressed by the agony of death do we finally turn to refuge.

Yet, having lived according to our desires, where can we now direct our minds? In frantic confusion, we lose our resolve and have no Dharma upon which to rely. We must willingly enter [the realms of suffering].
The three miserable realms are pitiable and lamentable; they are without support or protection, without destination or refuge.
Now, you have sent this ignorant one to inspire faith and seek rebirth, and to cause those with wisdom to resolve their doubts and awaken to the Way. All of us, from the beginningless past until now—
Lacking faith, they do not take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Western Quarter. They do not seek weary detachment from the five afflictions of this turbid world.

Failing to realize that delusions and karmic actions arise from their own minds, they commit the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds, break their fasts, violate the precepts, and accumulate all manner of unwholesome states.
That they have wandered through the cycle of birth and death until this very day is entirely due to their failure, since time immemorial, to awaken, to know, to hear, and to see. They did not...
Though they have relied upon teachers and friends, they have not encountered the scriptural teachings and do not understand cause and effect.

They give rise to groundless slander, practicing it themselves and teaching others to do so, while rejoicing when they see others do the same. Driven by karmic obstructions, they lack all faith and acceptance.

Through these various causes and conditions of hindrance, they obstruct the practice of rebirth [in the Pure Land], sever the seed of Buddhahood, fall away from the sacred embryo, and drift and sink into the evil realms, such that there will be no end to their future births and deaths.

There will come a time when our lives end; we shall fail to attain rebirth in the Pure Land and fail to achieve liberation. All this is due to being entangled by our own karmic offenses, mired in ignorance and delusion, and inverted in our views.
We do not believe in Amitābha Buddha; we do not believe in rebirth in the Pure Land. With our body, speech, and mind, we treat him with contempt and disparage him.

At times, upon seeing or hearing [of his name], we laugh it off with indifference; seeing others pay homage and recite his name, we harbor malicious intent and slander them, thereby destroying [the merit].
He is unwilling to encourage others to cultivate wholesome deeds and instead disturbs the practitioner. He praises false teachers;
even if one should believe him, one will vacillate between advancing and retreating, lacking a resolute mind. Though the body is at the site of practice, the mind dwells on worldly affairs;

though the mouth speaks of the Pure Land, the heart yearns for Jambudvīpa. Although the hands clutch a rosary, the mind harbors malice and evil. Thus, external conditions arise in profusion, both adverse and favorable.
Within their hearts, love and hatred arise in alternation; there are only empty words, entirely lacking in actual practice.
Merit has not been accumulated even by a hair’s breadth, while evil has already become a mountain. Without relying on the Three Refuges, it is difficult to eliminate the five fears.

Such offenses as these are immeasurable and boundless. We seek your compassion and perform this rite of repentance, praying that they may be extinguished. Let us together direct our minds with sincerity and equal, piercing earnestness. V.
Prostrating oneself to the ground, one takes refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.
With a sincere heart, one takes refuge in all the Buddha-Jewels of the Western Pure Land, the World of Ultimate Bliss.
(One prostration) With a sincere heart, one takes refuge in all the Dharma-Jewels of the Western Pure Land, the World of Ultimate Bliss. (One prostration)
With a sincere heart, I take refuge in all the Sangha Jewels of the Western Pure Land, the World of Ultimate Bliss. (One prostration) To the Triple Gem of the West,
we and all sentient beings, with a sincere heart, take refuge and pay homage,
vowing to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Furthermore, take refuge in all the Triple Gem and infinite worthy sages of the Western Pure Land,
the World of Ultimate Bliss (one prostration). Today,
the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice, with renewed sincerity and single-minded devotion, listen attentively to the *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*.
Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One, how many non-retrogressive bodhisattvas from this Sahā world will be reborn in the land of the Buddha of Infinite Life?
The Buddha told Maitreya, "In this world, there are six billion seven hundred million non-retrogressive bodhisattvas who will be reborn in that land.
Each and every one of these bodhisattvas has already made offerings to various Buddhas. Next...
Such as Maitreya. The number of bodhisattvas of minor practice and those who have cultivated few merits is beyond calculation;
all shall attain rebirth there. It is not only the bodhisattvas of my own land who attain rebirth;

in the immeasurable Buddha-lands of the worlds of the ten directions, those who attain rebirth are exceedingly numerous and incalculable. As stated in the *Xiangfa jueyi jing*: "After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa..."

The True Dharma shall endure for five hundred years, during which the observance of the precepts will be firm. The Semblance Dharma shall endure for one thousand years, during which meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) will be firm.

The Final Dharma shall endure for ten thousand years, during which the recollection of the Buddha (*buddhānusmṛti*) will be firm. According to the *Shijia beiwen* (Stele Inscription of Śākyamuni) in the *Fawang benji* (Record of the Original Account of the Dharma King), more than two thousand years have already passed, and several hundred years have elapsed since entering the Final Dharma period. Therefore, it should be known that this is precisely the time when sentient beings’ recollection of the Buddha will be firm.

The time for Amitābha to deliver sentient beings has arrived. As stated in the sutras, the roots and conditions of the sentient beings in this realm and ourselves, the great assembly, have reached maturity;

our capacities and responses correspond, and we have encountered this method of repentance. Thus, we shall be reborn in the Land of Immeasurable Life. Know that through the merit of reciting the Buddha’s name, blessings arise;

through the practice of prostrations and repentance, transgressions are extinguished. Those who seek birth in the Pure Land will, without exception, attain it. You should each faithfully believe the words of the Buddha.
Weary of this Sahā world and longing for the Land of Ultimate Bliss, we together with sincere resolve prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground.
We take refuge in the Great Compassionate One of the world;
we take refuge in all Buddhas throughout the ten directions and the entirety of empty space. (One prostration)
I take refuge in all the Honored Dharmas throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
(One prostration) I take refuge in all the worthy and holy ones throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
(One prostration) Vowing to be reborn together with all sentient beings in the Land of Peace and Bliss, I reverently pay homage with a sincere heart.
I take refuge once more in Amitābha Buddha of the West,
and likewise in all the Triple Gem and immeasurable worthies and sages throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space (one prostration).
Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice: The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* states that in this Sahā world, people together contend over matters that are not urgent.
Amidst such extreme evil and intense suffering, they labor their bodies in worldly affairs to provide for themselves.
Whether noble or lowly, poor or wealthy, young or old, male or female, all alike worry over wealth; whether one has it or lacks it, the anxiety is the same. Worry...

Their thoughts are constantly disturbed by such things as these, and they are simultaneously beset by sorrow and suffering. Their reflections and anxieties serve as the servants of their minds, leaving them no time of peace.

Their minds always contemplate evil, their mouths always speak evil, and their bodies always perform evil; there has never been a single good deed. They do not believe in the scriptures and teachings of the former sages and Buddhas;
they do not believe that by practicing the Way one can attain deliverance from the world; and they do not believe that after death, the spirit undergoes rebirth. They do not...
Believing that performing good brings good and committing evil brings evil, their hearts become obstructed and their minds fail to find liberation.

When their great life is about to end, remorse and fear arrive together; yet they did not practice goodness beforehand, only regretting at the moment of death. What can be achieved by regretting afterwards?

Such is the case for worldly people, which cannot be fully detailed here; thus, they naturally undergo immeasurable suffering and affliction in the three miserable realms, revolving from one to another.
Within this, for lifetimes spanning many kalpas, there is no time of emergence; liberation is difficult to attain, and its pain is beyond description.
These are the five great evils, the five pains, and the five burnings. The diligent suffering is like this: it is as if a great fire were burning a person's body.

You—whether among the gods, the people of the present, or those of future generations—who have obtained the words of the Buddha’s sutras, should reflect upon them deeply. You must be able to [act accordingly] within them...

Within this [world], to maintain a focused mind and upright conduct, observing the precepts with purity for one day and one night, is superior to practicing virtue for a hundred years in the Land of Immeasurable Life.
Why is this? Because that Buddha-land is unconditioned and spontaneous, where all manner of goodness is accumulated and not even a hair’s breadth of evil exists.
The Buddha said: "I have compassion for you, gods and humans, even more than parents cherish their children."
My son, now that I have attained Buddhahood in this world, I have subdued and transformed the five evils, eliminated the five pains, and extinguished the five burnings.

It is fitting that each and every person should reverently follow and uphold these teachings with sincere devotion. Together, with a focused mind, prostrate yourselves with your five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.
I take refuge in all Buddhas throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
(One prostration) I take refuge in all Honored Dharmas throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space.
(One prostration) I take refuge in all worthy and holy ones throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of space. (One prostration)
May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss; With a sincere heart, I take refuge in and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Furthermore, I take refuge in the Triple Gem and all the infinite worthies and sages throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space.
(One prostration).

Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice has already completed the preliminary clarification of the afflictions of the Sahā world—the five pains and five burnings of wearying detachment.
Next, we shall joyfully seek the Land of Ultimate Bliss. With single-minded sincerity, take refuge in the Triple Gem and listen attentively to the *dhāraṇī*.

The *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra* states: At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus: "In the western direction lies the world of Sukhāvatī, where a Buddha currently resides named Amitābha.

If there are members of the fourfold assembly who can correctly receive and uphold the name of that Buddha, by virtue of this merit, when they are on the verge of death, Amitābha Buddha will immediately come to that person's side together with a great multitude, causing them—"
They shall behold them; having beheld them, they will immediately give rise to joy and gladness, and their merit will increase manifold.

By virtue of these causes and conditions, in whatever place they are born, they will forever be free from the defiled forms of the womb and desire, and will be spontaneously reborn within pure and wondrous precious lotus flowers.

Possessing great supernatural powers, his radiance was brilliant and majestic. At that time, all the Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges together praised that World of Peace and Bliss (the following verses are abbreviated;
where the sutra is extensive, all subsequent instances should be modeled after this).
The Buddhist tradition teaches that one should pay homage to the Triple Gem in the western direction. Both [traditions] hear and see from afar the *Sūtra of Immeasurable Life*, which says:

"The Buddha addressed Ānanda: 'Rise, adjust your robes once more, join your palms with reverence, and pay homage to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life and all the Tathāgatas of the lands of the ten directions, constantly praising and extolling that Buddha.'"

Unobstructed and unhindered. Thereupon, Ānanda rose, adjusted his robes, straightened his body, and facing west, joined his palms in reverence and prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground to pay homage to the Buddha Amitāyus.

He addressed him, saying, "World-Honored One, I pray that I may behold that Buddha’s Land of Peace and Bliss, as well as its assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas. As soon as he had spoken these words, the Buddha Amitāyus immediately emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated all the worlds of the Buddhas.

At that moment, Ānanda saw the majestic and towering majesty of the Buddha Amitāyus, like Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, rising high above all other worlds; his marks and signs and his radiant light shone everywhere. The fourfold assembly in this gathering all saw it at once, and they likewise saw this land.

It was thus. At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda and the Bodhisattva Maitreya: "Do you see all the subtle, wondrous, and pure natural objects within that land, from the ground upward as far as the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens?

Have you seen them all? Ānanda replied: "Indeed, I have seen them. "Do you also hear the Great Voice of Amitāyus Buddha proclaiming throughout all worlds to transform sentient beings? Ānanda replied: "Indeed, I have heard it.

"Do you also see the people of that land riding upon palaces made of the seven treasures, hundreds of thousands of *yojanas* in height, traveling everywhere through the ten directions without obstruction to make offerings to the Buddhas? They replied: "We have seen it," and so forth. (From the *Fuzi* [Clothing] section.)

Lady Vaidehī guides future beings who seek rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, as explained in the *Sixteen Contemplations Sūtra* (the *Sūtra on Contemplating the Buddha of Immeasurable Life* states:

At that time, Vaidehī, upon seeing the World-Honored Buddha, removed her own jeweled necklaces and prostrated herself, weeping and crying out to the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I pray only that the World-Honored One will extensively expound for me the state of being free from sorrow...")

"I shall go to be born in that place of bliss; I take no pleasure in this turbid and evil world of Jambudvīpa. In this turbid and evil world, hell-beings, hungry ghosts, and animals abound, and it is filled with a multitude of unwholesome things.

I vow that in the future I shall not hear evil sounds nor see evil people. Now, before the World-Honored One, I prostrate myself with my five limbs touching the ground, seeking mercy and repenting. I pray only that the Buddha-Sun may teach me to contemplate the realm of pure karma. At that time, the World-Honored One emitted a light from between his eyebrows.

That golden light shone everywhere throughout immeasurable worlds in the ten directions and returned to rest upon the crown of the Buddha’s head, where it transformed into a golden platform as large as Mount Sumeru. Within it, the pure and wondrous lands of the Buddhas of the ten directions all appeared. Some lands were composed of the seven treasures, and furthermore—

There are lands where they consist entirely of lotus flowers; there are lands like the palaces of the Lord of Sovereignty (Īśvara); and there are lands like crystal mirrors, in which the lands of the ten directions all appear.

There are such immeasurable Buddha-lands, magnificent and beautiful to behold, which [the Buddha] caused Vaidehī to see. Then Vaidehī said to the Buddha: "World-Honored One, although these Buddha-lands are pure and all possess radiance, I now desire to be born in the world of Ultimate Bliss (Sukhāvatī) where Amitābha Buddha dwells.

I only pray that the World-Honored One will teach me how to contemplate and teach me right concentration. At that time, the Buddha of Immeasurable Life stood in mid-air, with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta standing in attendance at his left and right. Then Vaidehī saw them.

Having prostrated at the feet of the Buddha Amitāyus, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, it is by the Buddha’s spiritual power that I have now been able to see the Buddha Amitāyus, the two Bodhisattvas, and that land.

After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, when sentient beings are defiled, evil, unwholesome, and oppressed by the five sufferings, how shall they be able to see Amitābha Buddha and the world of Ultimate Bliss? The Buddha said: "Excellent! You have asked this matter well. Ānanda, you should receive and uphold these words of the Buddha, and proclaim them extensively for the sake of the great multitude.

Now, the Tathāgata instructs Vaidehī and all sentient beings of future ages to contemplate the world of Ultimate Bliss in the western quarter. By the power of the Buddha, they shall be able to see that Pure Land."

It is like holding up a bright mirror and seeing one’s own reflection; by seeing the supreme and wondrous joys of that land, the mind becomes filled with joy, and at that very moment, one attains the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

The Buddha told Vaidehī: "You are an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*), and your mental conceptions are weak and inferior. You have not yet attained the divine eye (*divyacakṣus*) and cannot see from afar. The Tathāgatas possess extraordinary skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) to enable you to see. The Buddha told Vaidehī:

"You and all sentient beings should single-mindedly fix your attention on one place and contemplate the West. How should you form this contemplation? Generally speaking, among all sentient beings, unless one is born blind, those who possess eyes all see the sun set. You should therefore give rise to this visualization: sit upright facing west and gaze intently at the sun, causing it..."

The mind remains firm and steadfast; one focuses the visualization without wavering. Seeing the sun about to set, its form is like a suspended drum. Having seen the sun, whether with eyes closed or open, one ensures it remains clear and distinct. This is the visualization of the sun, called the First Contemplation.

Next, one performs the contemplations of water, earth, and trees, continuing through to the sixteenth contemplation of the lower grade, as extensively described in the Sūtra. At that time, when the World-Honored One spoke these words, Vaidehī and her five hundred attendants, upon hearing what the Buddha had said, immediately beheld at that very moment the vast and expansive appearance of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

They beheld the body of the Buddha and the two Bodhisattvas, their hearts filled with joy and marveling at such an unprecedented occurrence. They attained sudden and great awakening, reaching the stage of the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). The five hundred attendants likewise resolved their minds toward Bodhi.

"May they be born in that land. The World-Honored One granted them all the prediction that they shall all go to be born there. Those who practice this samādhi will, in their present bodies, behold Amitāyus Buddha and the two Great Beings. Merely hearing the name of the Buddha and the names of the two Bodhisattvas eliminates the sins of birth and death accumulated over immeasurable kalpas;

how much more so for those who maintain mindfulness of them! If one recollects the Buddha, you should know that such a person is a *puṇḍarīka* (white lotus) among men, with Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta as their supreme friends. They shall sit at the site of enlightenment and be born into the family of all Buddhas. (From the Qi edition)
Those who commit evil and meet an untimely death, If they recite the Buddha’s name or make offerings, Their lifespan will be increased once more.

As stated in the *Śrī-ārya-amitāyur-dhyāna-tathāgata-vyuha-sūtra* (The Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Holy Infinite Life, Resolute Radiance King Tathāgata): The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying: "In this world of Jambudvīpa today, the human lifespan is one hundred years. Among them, there are many..."
Having committed various evil deeds, they meet with an untimely death. Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, if there are sentient beings who obtain sight of this sutra, its merit is exceptionally sublime;

and as for those who hear its name—if such short-lived persons wholeheartedly transcribe, receive, uphold, recite, offer worship to, and prostrate before it—such people shall have their lifespans increased, reaching a full hundred years. If one can maintain the recitation one hundred and eight times, the lifespan of such short-lived sentient beings will likewise be increased.
Furthermore, even those who merely hear its name and wholeheartedly believe, accept, honor, and revere it shall also attain an increase in their lifespan. (From the Engraved Edition)
For those who fear local officials, by reciting the names of these two Bodhisattvas, they shall be liberated from the calamity of fear.

As stated in the *Great Sūtra of Amitābha* (*The Sūtra of the Buddha Amitābha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Who Transfers Mankind Beyond [Suffering]*): The Buddha said, "Among the people of the world, if there are good men or good women who encounter urgent difficulties or fear regarding matters involving local officials, they need only..."
I take refuge in this Pavilion of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Lokeśvara; there is no one who does not attain liberation. (From the character "出服" [chūfú] series).
In the past, there was an assembly of four hundred million who vowed to be born in the Land of No Desire;

they simultaneously beheld the Pure Land, as described in the *Daśabhūmika-vistara-vidarśana-saṃyukta-sūtra* (The Scripture on Severing the Bonds of the Ten Abodes). It says: "At that time, the World-Honored One emitted the radiance of the Samādhi of the Awakened Flower’s Intent. An assembly of four hundred million saw these auspicious colors and each conceived a sense of weary detachment. They reflected within themselves: 'Birth is inevitably followed by death; all..."

"By means of causes and conditions, one dies here and is born there, linked together in an unbroken chain. Desire is the source; this arises from craving. We vow to be born in a land free of desire, so that we may cultivate this Samādhi of Awakening Mind.

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of those assembled, addressed them, saying: "To the west of here, beyond incalculable Buddha-lands, there is a Buddha named Amitāyus. His land is pure and free from lust, anger, and delusion. All share a single mind and are all born from within lotus flowers, not born of the passions of parents.

They are exclusively youths; there are no women. There is no excrement or urine; they take the joy of the Dharma of meditative liberation as their food. They are without conceptual thought or consciousness, and they regard one another with mutual respect, as if toward a father."

"Those who wish to be born there, like a mother [desiring her child], may now make a vow. At that time, the assembly of four hundred million beings, with one mind, made a vow to seek birth in that land. Thereupon, the World-Honored One, through the radiance of the Samādhi of Enlightened Mind, illuminated that land, the Tathāgata-World-Honored One, and the bodhisattvas born by transformation.

That land was widely renowned, interspersed with various jewels, and free from the sufferings of the three evil paths and the eight difficulties. Having seen that land, these four hundred million people, according to their physical forms and lifespans, were all simultaneously born in that land. (From the *Neng* edition)
When sentient beings mindfully recite the name of Amitābha, the Bodhisattvas will constantly provide protection; ghosts and spirits shall find no opportunity to harm them.
As stated in the *Ten Recitations Sutra*:

"The Ritual for Repentance and Worship" (*Lichan yi*) quotes the *Sutra of the Ten Ways of Rebirth*, saying: 'If there are sentient beings who mindfully recite the name of Amitābha Buddha and vow to be reborn [in his land], that Buddha will immediately dispatch twenty-five Bodhisattvas to protect and guard these practitioners, whether they are walking, standing, or sitting.'
Whether lying down, by day or by night, at all times and in all places, it shall not allow evil ghosts or malevolent spirits to find any opportunity against them. (From the Dingzi Edition)
There was a maiden named Shanxiang (Good Appearance) who, weary of the turbid world, paid homage toward the Western Quarter. Through the power of the Buddha, she was transformed into a man.
(*Jinglü yixiang* states:

When the Buddha was in Śrāvastī, there was the daughter of an elder named Shanxin (Good Faith). She was fifteen years of age, compassionate and filial by nature, and possessed of penetrating wisdom. From her youth, she had always maintained a great vow and took no pleasure in worldly affairs.)

As she sat reflecting on these matters, she thought: "All things are impermanent; they must return to death. Even a lifespan of ten thousand years ends in death, and even heaven and earth shall perish—how much more so the human body? After death, the soul and spirit shall enter the evil realms, where one must alone endure bitter poisons and arduous suffering.
From whence did this arise? Suddenly there is anger, terror, grief, and anxiety, or at times joy. Such are the affairs of impermanence. One does not see when it comes, nor where it goes.

These beings come and go without rest or pause. I think of my parents, my brothers, and my relatives both near and far; they do not know of sin or merit, and their greed for desire knows no satiety. When I was three or five years old, I was betrothed to another man. My brothers and family members feasted on rice, wine, and meat."

Having accepted this bolt of silk, my body shall surely undergo suffering and hardship; bound by material things, I cannot escape them. What shall I do? Rather than being subject to this birth and old age, it would be better for me to take advantage of this day’s purity and make a supreme vow.

He sought a palace of peace and eternal joy where he might find delight for himself; it was not fitting that he should be defiled by turbidity and sink into the three miserable realms (*trāya*), failing to behold the light and remaining forever conjoined with suffering. He then straightened his mind and made a vow: "I shall take my own body and life as witness;

there must surely be a deity and a spiritual power that knows the sincerity of my heart. At that moment, a celestial deity appeared in the void and spoke to Shanxin, saying: "If you would truly take refuge in the Western Land of Peace, Security, and Purity, you should first direct your worship toward the ten directions."

With a mind of loving-kindness and respectful reverence, he thought, "He will surely arrive. Once [the deity] had vanished, the faithful man leaped for joy and, having bathed himself, burned incense, scattered flowers, and prostrated toward the ten directions, joined his palms and meditated upon all people.
Immediately, a celestial deity spoke from the midst of the void: "You should, with a right mind, face the west and recite this one verse; by doing so, you shall praise Amitābha Buddha.
Following the deity's instruction, the Buddha and the great assembly then flew to the house of Shanxin, where [the deity] manifested as a man before the Buddha.

Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice, with one mind and sincerity, prostrate themselves with their five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.
Homage to the Teacher Śākyamuni Buddha!

homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva;
homage to the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the Pure Great Ocean.
Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Three Jewels and immeasurable worthies and sages throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space (one prostration).
O great assembly of fellow practitioners at this present site of enlightenment, may we, the disciples [Name] and others, from this day forth until we sit upon the path to enlightenment...
[The practitioner] contemplates the five pains and five burnings of the Sahā world with weary detachment, and seeks with joy the three refuges and the Triple Gem of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Following their vow, they aspire to be reborn in the Western Pure Land. Having made this vow, they take refuge and pay homage to all the Triple Gems of the Western Pure Land.
The Ritual for Repentance at the Meditation Hall of Amitābha, Scroll One. *Tá* (pronounced as in "tā"); *rǒng* (rhyme with *ér* and *luáng*);

*sī guò* (the first character is read in the upper tone); *suì* (pronounced as in "suì"); *shì* (pronounced as in "shì"); *gǒu* (pronounced as in "gǒu"); *kuí* (pronounced as in "kuí"); *pì* (rhyme with *pǔ* and *jī*); *yì* (pronounced as in "yì"); *lì* (pronounced as in "lì");

*bù shèng* (pronounced as in "shèng," meaning "to raise"; subsequent instances are to be understood accordingly); *shì* (pronounced as in "shì"); *jù* (rhyme with *qí* and *jù*, meaning "urgent"); *xùn* (pronounced as in "xùn"); *háng* (rhyme with *hú* and *láng*).
