Section Nine: The Gate of Seeking Birth.
With sincere resolve and deep mind, one dedicates [merit] through vows;
Abstaining from killing, observing the precepts, reciting the Mahāyāna, and practicing the six mindfulnesses, one is welcomed by transformation Buddhas.

This is called the "Highest Birth of the Highest Grade. (The *Sūtra on the Visualization of Infinite Life* states: "Ānanda and Vaidehī, as for those of the highest grade of the highest birth: if there are sentient beings who wish to be born in that land, they shall attain rebirth by giving rise to three kinds of minds. What are these three? First,")

First, the mind of sincere resolve; second, the profound mind; third, the mind of dedication and aspiration. Those who possess these three minds will certainly be born in that land. Furthermore, there are three kinds of sentient beings who shall attain rebirth there. What are the three?

First, those who possess a heart of compassion and do not kill, and who fulfill all the precepts and practices. Second, those who read and recite the Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras. Third, those who practice the six mindfulnesses and dedicate their merit through aspiration, vowing to be born in that land. If they possess these merits for even one day up to seven days, [they shall be born there].

One immediately attains rebirth in that land. Because this person has been diligent and courageous, Amitābha Tathāgata, together with Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, countless transformation Buddhas, hundreds of thousands of bhikṣus, the great assembly of śrāvakas, and immeasurable devas, as well as palaces made of the seven treasures, appear before the practitioner.

Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, holding a vajra platform, arrives before the practitioner along with Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva. Amitābha Buddha emits a great radiance that illuminates the practitioner’s body and extends his hands to welcome them.

Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and countless bodhisattvas praise the practitioner and encourage their resolve. Upon seeing this, the practitioner leaps for joy; they see themselves mounting the vajra platform and following after the Buddha.

Afterwards, in the time it takes to snap one's fingers, they will be reborn in that land. Having been born in that land, they will see the Buddha’s physical body, complete with all its marks; they will see the bodhisattvas, their forms and features fully perfected, amidst groves of radiant jewels as they proclaim the sublime Dharma.

Upon hearing this, they will immediately realize the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). In a mere moment, they will travel to serve various Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions, receiving successive predictions of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*) in the presence of those Buddhas. Returning to their original land, they will attain immeasurable hundreds of thousands of *dhāraṇī* gates. This is called the highest of the high grades of rebirth.

It is not necessary to uphold the Vaipulya sutras; If one understands the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*) and clarifies cause and effect, Seeing the entire body upon the purple-golden dais— This is called one of the highest grade of those born through middle-level practice.

(The Sutra says: "It is not necessary to uphold, recite, or chant the Vaipulya scriptures. If one understands their meaning and intent, and regarding the ultimate truth, the mind is not startled or shaken, deeply believes in cause and effect, and does not slander the Mahāyāna, then by virtue of these merits, one dedicates them toward making this aspiration.")

One shall be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. When the life of one who practices this path is about to end, Amitābha Buddha, surrounded by a vast assembly of followers including Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, will arrive before that practitioner holding a purple-golden pedestal.

He will praise them, saying: "O Son of the Dharma, you have practiced the Mahāyāna and understood the ultimate truth; therefore, I now come to welcome you. Together with a thousand transformation Buddhas, they will simultaneously extend their hands. The practitioner will see themselves seated upon the purple-golden pedestal, joining their palms in reverence and praising the Buddhas.

In the space of a single thought-moment, they will be born in that land within the ponds of the seven treasures. This purple-golden pedestal is like a great jewel-flower, which opens after one night has passed. The practitioner’s body becomes the color of purple-polished gold, and beneath their feet there are also the seven...

Upon jeweled lotuses, the Buddha and the Bodhisattvas simultaneously emit light that illuminates the practitioner’s body; their eyes immediately open and become clear. Due to their prior habitual practice, they universally hear various sounds purely expounding the profound, supreme ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*).

They then descend from the golden platform, prostrate before the Buddha with palms joined, and praise the World-Honored One. After seven days have passed, at that very moment, they attain non-retrogression regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. At that very moment, they are able to fly and travel everywhere throughout the ten directions to serve all Buddhas. In the presence of these Buddhas, they cultivate various *samādhis*.

After the passing of one small kalpa, they attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and receive a face-to-face prediction of enlightenment. This is called the "one born of the superior grade."
With deep faith in cause and effect, one upholds the Mahāyāna;

Merely by giving rise to the unsurpassed bodhicitta, Upon hearing the Dharma, one ascends to the first stage of the ten bhūmis. This is called one who attains birth in the lower grade of the superior class. (The Sūtra says:

"One also believes in cause and effect and does not slander the Mahāyāna, giving rise to the mind of the unsurpassed path. By dedicating these merits toward the aspiration to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, when the practitioner’s life is about to end, Amitābha Buddha and Avalokiteśvara... )

Śrīkṣetra, together with his retinue, holding purple-gold lotus flowers, manifests as five hundred Buddhas to welcome this person. These five hundred manifested Buddhas simultaneously extend their hands and praise him, saying:

"O son of the Dharma, you are now pure; having resolved upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment, I have come to welcome you. When he sees this, he perceives himself sitting upon a golden lotus flower. Once seated, the flower closes, and following behind the World-Honored One, he immediately attains rebirth within a pool of the seven treasures.

After one day and one night, the lotus flower opens; within seven days, he is able to see the Buddha. Although he beholds the Buddha’s body, his mind is not yet clear regarding the various marks and signs of excellence. After twenty-one days, he finally perceives them clearly. He hears various sounds, all of which expound the wondrous Dharma, as he travels through the ten [directions].

They shall make offerings to all Buddhas and, in the presence of those Buddhas, hear the profound Dharma. After three minor kalpas, they will attain the "Gate of Illumination of the Hundred Dharmas" and dwell on the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*). These are called those who are born in the lower grade of the highest class; this is termed the perception of birth in the highest class.
This is the fourteenth visualization.

"Those who uphold the five precepts and the eightfold fast, who practice all the various precepts and dedicate their merit toward the vow to see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and realize the stage of No-more-learning— these are called those of the middle grade who are born in the highest level [of Sukhāvatī].

(The Sūtra says: If there are sentient beings who uphold the five precepts, observe the eightfold fast, and practice all the various precepts; who do not commit the five heinous crimes and are free from all faults and afflictions; and who, by means of these roots of goodness, dedicate them toward the vow to be born in the World of Ultimate Bliss—at the time of their death..."

At the time of death, Amitābha Buddha, surrounded by a retinue of bhikṣus, emits golden light and arrives at the person’s side. He expounds upon suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self, and praises the life of renunciation as the means to escape all sufferings.

Upon seeing this, the practitioner’s heart is filled with great joy; he sees himself seated upon a lotus pedestal, kneeling with palms joined in prostration before the Buddha. Before his head has even been raised, he attains rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. The lotus flower immediately opens, and as it blooms, he hears various sounds praising the Four Noble Truths.

At that moment, he attains the path of Arhatship, endowed with the three knowledges, the six supernatural powers, and the eight liberations. This is called the highest grade of the middle class of rebirth.

If a person, with a sincere heart, for one day and one night, observes the precepts and the fast without breach or flaw, and upon hearing the Dharma immediately attains the stage of *srotāpanna*, this is called one born in the middle grade of the middle class.

(The Sūtra says: "If there are sentient beings who, for one day and one night, receive and uphold the eightfold fast, or for one day and one night uphold the *śrāmaṇera* precepts, or for one day and one night uphold the full precepts (*upasaṃpad*), their majestic demeanor being without flaw—by this merit..."

Virtue. One should dedicate [this merit] with the vow to seek birth in Sukhāvatī, perfuming oneself with the fragrance of the precepts. For such a practitioner, when life is about to end, they will see Amitābha Buddha together with his retinue, emitting golden light and holding a lotus flower made of the seven treasures, appearing before the practitioner.

The practitioner will personally hear a voice from the air praising them, saying: "O son of good family! Because you, a person of virtue, have followed the teachings of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, I have come to welcome you. The practitioner will personally see themselves seated upon the lotus flower;

as soon as it closes, they will be born in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss within a jeweled pond. After seven days have passed, the lotus flower will open. Once the flower has opened, the practitioner will open their eyes, join their palms, and praise the World-Honored One. Hearing the Dharma, they will rejoice and attain...
The *srotāpanna*, after half a kalpa has passed, becomes an *arhat*. This is called "one born in the middle grade within the middle birth.
Filial in supporting one's parents and practicing benevolence and compassion, one encounters a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) at the time of death;
reborn through transformation, one realizes the stage of no-more-learning (*aśaikṣa*) within one kalpa. This is called "one born in the lower grade within the middle birth."

The Sūtra says: "If there are good sons or good daughters who filially support their parents and practice worldly benevolence and compassion, when such a person’s life is about to end, they will encounter a spiritual friend who will extensively explain for them the joyful matters of Amitābha Buddha’s land."

He also spoke of the forty-eight vows of the Bhikṣu Dharmākara. Having heard this matter, he immediately passed away. Like a strong man extending or contracting his arm, he was reborn in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss. Seven days after his birth, he encountered Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta;

hearing the Dharma, he rejoiced. After the passing of one small kalpa, he became an Arhat. This is called the "Lower Birth of the Middle Grade. This is called the perception of birth in the Middle Class. It is known as the Fifteenth Meditation.

If a person, though not slandering the honored sutras, commits various evil karmas and lacks shame or remorse, yet is born by transformation after ten kalpas in the first stage of the ten bhūmis—this is called one who attains birth in the superior grade of the lower level.

(The Sutra says: "There may be sentient beings who commit various evil karmas; although they do not slander the Vaipulya sutras, such deluded people create many unwholesome dharmas and possess no shame or remorse. When their lives are about to end, they encounter a virtuous friend who speaks for them... )

The titles of the twelve divisions of the Mahāyāna sūtras: by hearing the names of these various sūtras, one eliminates the extremely heavy evil karma of a thousand kalpas. Furthermore, the wise teacher instructs [the practitioner] to join the palms and press the hands together, reciting "Namo Amitābha Buddha.

By reciting the Buddha’s name, the offenses of fifty billion kalpas of birth and death are eliminated. At that time, that Buddha immediately dispatches transformation Buddhas, transformation Avalokiteśvara, and transformation Mahāsthāmaprāpta before the practitioner, praising them, saying:

"Good son, because you have recited the Buddha’s name, all your offenses are extinguished; I come to welcome you. Having spoken these words, the practitioner immediately beholds the radiance of the transformation Buddhas filling his room. Having seen this, he rejoices and then passes away, riding upon a precious lotus flower, following...

After the emanation Buddha has departed, they are born within a precious lotus pond. After seven weeks have passed, the lotus flower finally blooms. At that time, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta emit great radiance and stand before the person, preaching the profound twelvefold scriptures for them.

Having heard this, they believe and understand it, giving rise to the mind set on the unsurpassed path. After ten minor kalpas, they become endowed with the gate of illumination of the hundred dharmas and attain entry into the first stage (bhūmi). This is called "Birth in the Higher Grade of the Lower Class."

If there are sentient beings who violate the various precepts, steal the property of the Saṃgha or the Three Jewels, yet suddenly entrust themselves to a precious lotus by mindfulness of the Buddha—these are called those born in the middle grade of the lower level.

(The Sūtra says: "If there are sentient beings who destroy and violate the five precepts or the full precepts; such foolish people as these steal the property of the Saṃgha, pilfer the goods of the present Saṃgha, preach the Dharma with impurity, and lack shame or remorse; because of these various evil karmas... )
Self-Adornment: Such a sinner, due to their evil karma, ought to fall into hell. When their life is about to end, the various fires of hell arrive all at once.

Yet, they encounter a virtuous friend who, out of great compassion, explains for them the majesty and power of Amitābha Buddha throughout the ten directions, extensively praising that Buddha’s radiant spiritual power, as well as his precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation. Upon hearing this, the person eliminates the offenses of eighty billion kalpas of birth and death.

The fierce fires of hell transform into cool, refreshing breezes, which blow heavenly flowers; upon each flower are manifested Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who welcome the person. In the space of a single thought-moment, they attain rebirth within a lotus flower inside a pond of the seven treasures. There they remain for six kalpas.

The lotus then blooms. Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, with voices of Brahmā, comfort those people and preach for them the profound Mahāyāna sūtras. Having heard this Dharma, they immediately give rise to the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment at that very moment.
This is called the "lowest grade of middle birth."
If one commits the five heinous crimes or the ten evil deeds, one should fall into hell and undergo all manner of suffering;
yet if, at the moment of death, one recollects the Buddha, one will likewise transcend [rebirth]—this is called the lowest grade of birth in the lower level.

(The Sūtra says: "There may be sentient beings who commit unwholesome karma—the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds—fully possessing such unwholesome karma. Such foolish people, because of their evil karma, should fall into the evil realms and undergo inexhaustible suffering for many kalpas. Thus it is said.)

When an evil person approaches the end of life and encounters a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), who provides various forms of consolation and explains the sublime Dharma to them, instructing them to practice mindfulness of the Buddha; yet this person, oppressed by suffering, has no leisure to practice such mindfulness. The virtuous friend tells them: "If you cannot practice mindfulness of the Buddha, you should instead recite the name of Amitāyus Buddha.

Thus, with sincere resolve, they cause the sound not to cease, completing ten recitations while calling out, "Namo Amitābha Buddha. Because of reciting the Buddha’s name, in every single thought-moment (*citta-kṣaṇa*), the sins of eighty billion kalpas of birth and death are eliminated.

At the time of death, they see a golden lotus flower, like a sun-disk, appearing before them. In the space of a single thought-moment, they attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Within that lotus flower, they remain for twelve great kalpas.

As the lotus flower begins to open, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, with voices of great compassion, extensively expound for them the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena and the methods for extinguishing sinful karma. Having heard this, they rejoice; immediately at that moment, they give rise to the bodhicitta.
This is called "those of the lowest grade who are born [in the Pure Land]"; it is called the "conception of being born as the lowest class"; and it is called the sixteenth visualization.
Today, the great assembly, following the *Sūtra of the Sixteen Contemplations* as taught by the Buddha, shall together cultivate the nine grades of practice for seeking rebirth.
With sincere resolve, we prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

The Ninth Fascicle of the Ritual for Repentance at the Altar of Contemplating Amitābha:
Supplement to the Practices for Seeking Rebirth.
If a person sits upright facing true west, constantly recollecting the Buddha throughout ninety days.
"One can achieve samādhi and be born before the Buddha," so says Mañjuśrī in the *Prajñāpāramitā*.

"If a person single-mindedly recollects a Buddha of one direction, whether walking or sitting, after seven weeks they will see their own body and see the Buddha, and thus attain rebirth there. So it is said in the *Mahāsannipāta Sūtra*.
For ten days and ten nights, one seeks through fasting and purification;
Hanging silk banners and canopies, burning incense and lamps, with continuous mindfulness, one attains rebirth there. The *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra* speaks thus:
"For ten days and ten nights, during the six periods [of the day and night], One prostrates with the five limbs while maintaining uninterrupted mindfulness."
"One sees that Buddha manifest and is immediately reborn there," as stated in the *Drum-Sound King Sūtra*.
"Whether for one day, two days, or seven days, if one holds the Name with an undistracted mind,
the Buddha will appear before them and they shall be reborn there," as stated in the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra*.

Today, the great assembly, as taught in the sutras, seeks the practice for rebirth. With a sincere heart, we prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

all attain purity of the three karmas, give rise to the bodhicitta, and realize the path of liberation. (Name), and others, look up to and rely upon the power of the great vows of Amitābha Buddha,
the power of the practices and vows of all the great Bodhisattvas and worthy sages— immeasurable and inexhaustible.
The power of wisdom; the power of merit; the power of sovereign supernormal faculties; the power of protecting sentient beings; the power of comforting sentient beings;
the power of exhausting the outflows of all devas and rishis; the power of gathering and transforming all roots of goodness;
the power of rescuing sentient beings from the hells; the power of delivering all hungry ghosts; the power of liberating all animals; [and] causing all sentient beings...

May these vows be fulfilled. May the meritorious roots and supreme causes—from the initial taking of refuge in the Triple Gem by [Name] and others, up to their prostrations before the Buddha—cause all sentient beings to attain their aspirations.

Furthermore, may [Name] and others rely upon the power of the great compassion of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter, the power of the great compassionate mind of the Buddhas of the ten directions, and the Buddhas of the six directions.
The power of the Great Compassionate One’s mind; the power of the thirty-five Buddhas to extinguish afflictions; the power of the fifty-three Buddhas to subdue the Māras;
the power of the one hundred and seventy Buddhas to deliver sentient beings; the power of the thousand Buddhas to gather in and sustain all sentient beings;

the power of the nine hundred and ninety million Buddhas to bring about accomplishment; and the power of the repentance rites propagated by Avalokiteśvara and Samantabhadra—may these cause all sentient beings to attain [suchness].

The Tenth Fascicle of the Ritual for Repentance at the Amitābha Dharma-Assembly;
Part Eleven: Self-Rejoicing.
Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice has collectively completed its prostrations to the Buddha.
May all sentient beings together receive liberation: those of the past have already attained rebirth; those of the present shall attain rebirth;
and those of the future, by practicing according to this, shall likewise attain rebirth. Now, you should rejoice; let the assembly leap for joy and [celebrate] one another.

(One prostration).
Today, if the great assembly knows how to rejoice for themselves, they must further cultivate the supramundane mind. Why is this self-rejoicing? The Buddha said:
"Hell is difficult to escape from; we have all together already attained liberation from this suffering. This is the first [reason for rejoicing].
"Joy! We have already escaped the suffering of the hungry ghosts; this is our first self-congratulation.
We have already escaped the difficulty of being abandoned by fellow animals and shall no longer receive their retribution; this is our second self-congratulation.

Born in a remote land where benevolence and righteousness were unknown, we have already attained residence in the Central Kingdom where the Way and its laws circulate, and we personally receive the sublime teachings; this is [our third self-congratulation]."

Fourth, we rejoice that we have been born in the Heaven of Long Life; unaware of how to plant the seeds of merit, we have now already attained this state and shall further establish causes for ourselves.
This is the fifth self-rejoicing. Fifth, a human body is difficult to obtain; once lost, it cannot be regained. We have already obtained it, and each has acquired a human form.
This is the sixth self-rejoicing. Sixth, those with impaired faculties do not participate in the roots of goodness; we are pure together and have attained this profound Dharma-gate. This is...
Seventh, we rejoice that our worldly wisdom and eloquence have instead become a source of difficulty; together we take refuge with one mind in the True Dharma—this is the eighth ground for rejoicing.
The Buddha said, "To see a Buddha is difficult," yet we have already attained this; gazing upon the Honored Image—this is the ninth ground for rejoicing.
The Buddha said, "To hear the Dharma is likewise difficult," yet we have already attained this; partaking of the nectar of immortality—this is the tenth ground for rejoicing. The Buddha...

He said, "To leave the household life is difficult; you have already achieved this. To bid farewell to kin, sever your attachments, and turn toward the path of the Way—this is my eleventh cause for self-congratulation.
The Buddha said, "To benefit oneself is easy; to benefit others is difficult. Today, as you all perform one prostration and one salutation..."
"To universally benefit the ten directions—this is the twelfth self-congratulation. The Buddha said, "To endure toil and suffer hardship is difficult;
that you all today each exert yourselves with diligence and perform deeds not for your own sake—this is the thirteenth self-congratulation. The Buddha said:
"To recite and chant is difficult; that we, this great assembly, have together attained the ability to recite and chant is our fourteenth cause for self-congratulation.
To practice seated meditation is difficult; that we now see those whose minds are stilled and settled in concentration is our fifteenth cause for self-congratulation.
With unified resolve, leaping with joy, we prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World."

"Today, the great assembly—fifteen kinds as previously described—are those in the world who seek birth in the Pure Land;

this is the joy of cultivating the causes. Furthermore, you should know that there are another fifteen kinds who represent the joy of attaining rebirth in the Pure Land through transcending the world.
Each person should, with sincere resolve, collect the mind and listen attentively. The Buddha said: "This teaching is difficult to encounter, difficult to believe, and difficult to understand."
"Now that I have encountered this teaching, it is easy to believe and easy to understand; this is my sixteenth self-congratulation.

The Buddha said, "In previous lives I did not encounter this teaching, which is why I did not escape the cycle of birth and death within the three realms and six paths; this is my seventeenth self-congratulation. The Buddha said:
Sentient beings are turbid and evil; their obstacles are heavy and their merit is meager. Although this teaching exists, they are deluded and do not know it, or knowing it, they do not practice it.
Now, having encountered this teaching, they are able both to know it and to practice it—this is the eighteenth cause for self-congratulation. The Buddha said:

"Those who do not know this teaching cultivate various miscellaneous virtues, lacking a resolute mind, and thus do not escape saṃsāra. Now, having encountered this teaching, they cultivate one practice exclusively, with determination."

One escapes from saṃsāra; this is the nineteenth self-congratulation. The Buddha said: "Those who lack roots of goodness, at the time of their death, mostly see evil realms or encounter adverse conditions.
They do not hear the teachings of the sūtras, and being entangled by their sinful karma, they wail in terror as they enter hell, with no means to seek salvation.
Now, having received these instructions, at the time of death, they encounter favorable conditions and meet..."
A virtuous friend teaches them to practice this dharma, extensively expounding upon the excellent signs and supreme methods of the Western Pure Land, pointing each one out in detail.

Their hearts are filled with joy, and they make a vow to be reborn there. Alternatively, they may hear a virtuous friend teach the recitation of the ten invocations, or they themselves recite "Namo Amitābha Buddha" ten times in succession; as soon as these ten invocations are complete, the evil states [of mind] immediately...

When the state of cessation occurs and wholesome objects appear before them, the person will see Amitābha Buddha, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, and the assembly of the Pure Sea coming personally to welcome them.
They will either sit upon a lotus pedestal or ride upon a lotus flower, following behind the Buddha as they are reborn in the Pure Land.
This is the twentieth self-congratulation. Having been born in the Pure Land, there are the nine grades and four colors within the lotus ponds made of the seven treasures, which arise spontaneously.
21st self-congratulation: Having been born by transformation (*upapāduka*), one forms a pure body, free from the substance of a womb or egg. 22nd self-congratulation:
Having been born in the Pure Land, the body is of true golden color, endowed with the thirty-two marks, and its appearance is dignified and majestic, devoid of all ugliness.

Having been born in the Pure Land, one possesses the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), flying through space with mastery and traveling throughout the ten directions to perform [beneficial deeds].
This is the twenty-third self-congratulation: having been born in the Pure Land, one’s lifespan is immeasurable, equal to that of the Buddha, and there is no premature death.
This is the twenty-fourth self-congratulation: having been born in the Pure Land, clothing and food appear according to one’s thoughts, palaces follow the body, and there is natural happiness;
adorned with the seven treasures, everything is fully provided, and there is nothing one seeks that cannot be obtained.
Twenty-five: Self-congratulation. Having been born in the Pure Land, one possesses unimpeded eloquence and attains eighty-four thousand *dhāraṇī* gates;
one’s wisdom is clear and penetrating, with nothing that is not fully understood. This is twenty-six: Self-congratulation.
Having been born in the Pure Land, one has the great Bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta as supreme companions, and is free from association with those whom one hates. This is twenty—

Seventh, self-congratulation: Having been born in the Pure Land, one hears the Dharma during the six periods of the day and night and realizes the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharmakṣānti*).

This is the twenty-eighth self-congratulation. Having been born in the Pure Land, there is no further regression; one proceeds directly until the attainment of Buddhahood. This is the twenty-ninth self-congratulation.
Having perfected the power of patience, one boards the ship of great vows and returns to the triple world, traveling throughout the ten directions within the ocean of birth and death. Furthermore...
To deliver sentient beings, to be reborn in the Pure Land, and to together attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*— these are the thirty ways of self-congratulation.

the assembly of fellow practitioners in this *dharmaparyāya* site, we pray that through the merit produced by our disciples’ cultivation and dedication of these repentance rites,
may the present Emperor and the imperial family, from this day forth until they attain [Buddhahood], [enjoy peace and prosperity].
The site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). To uphold the Buddha-dharma like Sadāprarudita; to extinguish transgressions through great compassion like Ākāśagarbha;
to be able to hear the Dharma from afar like Vaidūryanirbhāsa; and to skillfully understand difficult teachings like Vimalagarbha.

Furthermore, may the parents from whom [so-and-so] and others were born, as well as all kinsmen throughout kalpas, from this moment until they sit at the site of enlightenment, disperse their forms throughout the realm of space like...
The Bodhisattva Anantagātra possesses ten merits. Just as the noble King Guṇaratna rejoiced upon hearing the Dharma, being free from fear;

and just as Mahāsthāmaprāpta is courageous in his supernormal powers—may [so-and-so] and others, including preceptors, ācāryas, fellow students, kinsmen, and all spiritual friends, whether of the upper, middle, or lower ranks, obtain each [of these qualities] from this moment until they reach the site of enlightenment.
Fearless as the lion king; manifesting great transformations like shadows and echoes, like the Jewel-Heap (Ratnakūṭa); hearing sounds to rescue from suffering, like Avalokiteśvara;

skillfully able to inquire and consult, like Mahākāśyapa. Furthermore, may [so-and-so] and others—whether monastics or laypeople, donors of faith, virtuous friends, or evil associates, along with their respective retinues—from this day forth until they reach the site of enlightenment, be liberated from all perils.

From calamity, he is like one who provides rescue and deliverance. In appearance, he is dignified and majestic, like Mañjuśrī. He is able to cast off karmic obstructions as if discarding the five hindrances (*āvaraṇa*).

Even when making his final offering, he is equal to Cunda. Furthermore, may all devas, rishis, and the Four Heavenly Kings who protect the world—wise, upright, and just—along with those who preside over the heavens, earth, and space, rewarding the good and punishing the evil, protect those who uphold this mantra. May the Dragon Kings of the five directions and their dragons...

The eight classes of deities, the spirits of the hidden and manifest realms, and their respective retinues: from this moment until the conclusion of this *dharmakṣetra*, may you all provide protection through great compassion.
May I practice with such diligence in upholding the Dharma that I never cease, like Rāhula; may my recitation and study be as far-reaching as Samantabhadra’s;
and may I burn my own body for the sake of the Dharma, like Bhaiṣajyarāja. Furthermore, I pray that all enemies and kin throughout the ten directions, and...
May all sentient beings— whether enemies, relatives, or neutral parties— of the four modes of birth and the six realms of existence, along with their respective retinues,
from this moment until they reach the site of enlightenment, have hearts free from attachment, like the woman Vimilā, and be as skillful in subtle and wondrous exposition as Queen Śrīmālā.
He is able to practice with diligence like Śākyamuni; his virtuous vows are equal to those of Amitāyus;
his majestic spiritual power is like that of the various heavenly kings; he is inconceivable like Vimalakīrti; and all his merits are individually perfected.

In all immeasurable Buddha-lands, every adornment is fully present. I look up with aspiration to the immeasurable Buddhas, the great Bodhisattvas, and all the worthy and holy ones throughout the entirety of the void realm of the ten directions;
may you, with hearts of compassion, together grant your protective acceptance, rescuing, guarding, and welcoming us.
May all aspirations be fulfilled; may their faith be firm and steadfast; and may their virtuous deeds increase daily.

May they nurture the four classes of beings with compassion as if each were their only child, causing all sentient beings to attain the four immeasurable minds and be endowed with the six *pāramitās*.
May they behold the Buddhas at will, just like Śrīmālā, and may all their practices and vows be ultimately accomplished, so that they may together with the Tathāgatas ascend to perfect enlightenment.
XIII. Entrusting the Propagation Now, as for this entrustment of the propagation:

it is to continue the life-force of Amitābha’s wisdom and to transmit the heart-lamp of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. The Dharma arises through conditions; the Way is manifested by persons. Within the teachings of Amitābha, this entrustment is proclaimed with gravity; within the *Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtras*, its circulation is extensively expounded.

Now that the Buddha has long departed and the age of the Final Dharma has arrived, we entrust this method of repentance to the ten directions and rely upon the Buddha’s power to circulate it through the myriad ages. We further pray for the secret protection of the dragons and devas and the hidden assistance of the worthy sages, so that [the Dharma] may advance.

The Way is free from demonic interference, ensuring that practitioners find reliance upon it. Humans and devas alike rejoice; all beings of water and land are filled with delight. Thus, they shall mutually transform one another in joy without end, successively propagating the profound mystery so that it endures imperishably. Whether hearing or seeing this, all shall go to the Western Land.

Whether receiving or upholding [this teaching], may all return to the Land of Ultimate Bliss. We pray that it may be transmitted without end throughout the ocean of kalpas, together aiding Amitābha as a guiding light.
Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice has already completed the universal dedication of merit. Next, we should entrust it for its circulation.
We look up with aspiration to all the sages and worthies of the ten directions and three periods of time, to Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, the Vajra-devas, and others.

May the assembly of Dharma-protecting deities cause this method of repentance to circulate without interruption throughout the limits of the future, extensively delivering all sentient beings and bringing great benefit to many.
Whether practicing it oneself or exhorting others, whether seeing, hearing, or rejoicing in it, or even copying, reading, reciting, and upholding it—may it be so.

We shall equally attain rebirth in the Western Pure Land. For this reason, we prostrate ourselves with our five limbs touching the ground and take refuge in the Great Compassionate Father of the World.

I speak these words of truth. You sentient beings should all believe and accept this Dharma-gate of inconceivable praise for the merits of the Buddha-fields, which is embraced by all Buddhas.

May I, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss; with a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Three Jewels and immeasurable worthies and sages throughout the entirety of the ten directions and the realm of empty space (one prostration).
Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of enlightenment, with renewed sincerity, entrusts this to you for its circulation. We look up and address the ten directions.

All Bodhisattvas throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space, and the Dharma-protecting Spirit Kings, by the power of their original vows, pledge to deliver sentient beings and gather them in, without end or limit. Like spiritual friends, they are free from discriminatory thoughts.
May all sentient beings come to know the kindness of the Tathāgata and draw near to him with offerings. May all Bodhisattvas regard them with compassion and pity, causing all sentient beings—

Having been born [in this state], I shall not contravene their teachings, but shall be able to receive and uphold them all without weariness or rest. Attaining the unobstructed vehicle, I shall reach ultimate sovereignty.

Beginning from taking refuge in the Triple Gem and ending with the entrustment for the circulation [of the Dharma], I dedicate all the merit of my repentance to all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm.
I look up with aspiration to the World-Honored One Amitābha and all Buddhas of the ten directions, who now manifest as...

I bear witness. May all my aspirations be fully accomplished. May all sentient beings together be born in the Pure Land, hear the Dharma and awaken to the Way, becoming fully endowed with merit and wisdom, equal in no way to the various Bodhisattvas. Entering the diamond-like mind, may they attain Equal and Perfect Enlightenment.
With mutual sincerity, prostrating with the five limbs touching the ground, we take refuge in the Great Compassionate One of the World.
Compassionate Father!
Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, the Teacher;
homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter; homage to Maitreya Buddha of the Future.

The Bodhisattva Śāntendriya, the Bodhisattva Jñānottara,
the Bodhisattva Sadāparihīṇaloka, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Vajragarbha Bodhisattva, Sadāparibhūta Bodhisattva,
Anikṣiptadhura Bodhisattva, Gadgadasvara Bodhisattva,
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and Ratnacandra Bodhisattva.
Homage to the Bodhisattva Candraprabha, the Bodhisattva Sadāprarudita, the Bodhisattva Trailokyasamatikrānta, and the Great Bhṛkuṭī-Tārā.

Homage to Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara; homage to Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
homage to the assembly of Bodhisattvas of the Pure Great Ocean.
Furthermore, I take refuge in all the Three Jewels and immeasurable worthy sages throughout the ten directions, as far as the limits of empty space.
(One prostration).

Today, the assembly of fellow practitioners at this site of practice: this Dharma gate of the Nianfo Liturgy for Rebirth has been practiced by the Bodhisattvas of the past and they have already been born in the Land of Peace and Bliss; it shall be practiced by the Bodhisattvas of the future, and they shall likewise be born there.
The Land of Bliss. The bodhisattvas currently present are now practicing it; having been born in the Land of Peace and Bliss this very life, we are fortunate to also practice this Dharma.

Thus, together with these bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, we shall assemble and travel through the pure Buddha-land of Ultimate Bliss, experiencing the most supreme and vast joy of the Dharma.
The *Commentary on the Amitābha Sūtra* states: "To exhort even one person to recite the Buddha's name..."
This is precisely the accomplishment of the rebirth of one sentient being. The rebirth of one sentient being is the accomplishment of that one sentient being’s attainment of Buddhahood.
Once one sentient being has attained Buddhahood, they immediately deliver immeasurable sentient beings to the attainment of Buddhahood.

Once immeasurable sentient beings have attained Buddhahood, they in turn deliver an infinite number of sentient beings to the attainment of Buddhahood. This is the excellence of the future Buddhas appearing in the world.

All causes originate from this. Therefore, the practice of the Amitābha Liturgy and Repentance Dharma-gate is the swift path to Buddhahood and the essential ford for transcending the world, through which one brings sentient beings to fulfillment and attains rebirth in the Pure Land. Its immeasurable merit is by no means a minor benefit.

Now, I shall open the treasury of jewels, point out the pearl within the garment, and entrust it to those with the karmic affinity, so that all may equally enjoy its use. I prostrate myself in reverence.
I take my leave. All pay homage. The ritual for repentance and the recitation of the name of Amitābha Buddha by the noble assembly of the Three Vehicles is hereby completed.

By these merits, may they be shared universally with all; may we and all sentient beings be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and together behold the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, all attaining the Way of the Buddhas.
May the merit of this work be redirected upward to assist the unconditioned transformation of the state.
We humbly pray that the present Emperor may live for ten thousand years.
May the civil and military officials enjoy a thousand autumns under the Heavenly Mandate.
May the Sage Sun shine as brightly as the Buddha-Sun;

may the Golden Wheel and the Dharma-Wheel revolve in tandem. May the winds be harmonious and the rains timely, ensuring bountiful harvests and peace in the seasons. May the myriad nations rejoice, and the four [quarters] [be at peace].

May the peripheries be tranquil; may those throughout the ten directions who harbor consciousness together become transformed births in Sukhāvatī, and may all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm collectively become part of Amitābha’s oceanic assembly.
Looking upward with reverence, we pray that the Great Awakened One will look down and grant his grace.
Verification. I reverently repent.
The Ritual for Repentance in the Meditation Hall of Amitābha, Scroll Ten (End).
Hǎn (pronounced hàn).
Formerly, Master Lang of Guishan early on cast off the tether of fame; today he is skilled in lecturing and is moreover sincere and filial. I respect him all the more.

In the second month of spring in the year of Yimao, he came and said to me: "I wish to use the Great Repentance (Dàchàn) to serve as a means for universal goodness, so that those of the final dharma age may enter the Buddha-way."

This is the end of the shortcut. During the Shun era, when the Tripitaka Master Shunan was residing in Yanjing, he had the text of this repentance ritual carved into printing blocks at Tian’an Temple so that it might be widely printed and circulated.
Unfortunately, the blocks were destroyed by fire in the year of Xinchou (1241), and I regretted their disappearance.

Fortunately, because the Master handled the matter of reprinting them, I rejoiced and assisted him. You intend to record a single phrase at the end [to avoid [the need for further commentary]), saying: "What?"
I venture to add these words. The Master smiled and departed. When I returned, I requested a colophon for the work; though he declined, he would not yet cease.
Thus, I cite this account to briefly stir the faith of those who follow the Buddha. Formerly, Luoseng Fazei resided at Xikong Temple; he was a bodhisattva of the world.
He vowed to cultivate the practices for the Pure Land for ten thousand days. When the period arrived, he indeed set out toward the West together with two thousand lay patrons.
It is clear, then, that "ten thousand people attaining passage together" is no mere saying; for the principle of the past and present is non-dual, and the person and the Dharma are likewise one.

There is only a difference in the depth of their faith and the diligence of their mindfulness. If one can possess deep faith in the Buddha and diligent mindfulness, [the goal will surely be attained].
When the faculties and objects are purified, one becomes a vessel for the Dharma; thus, at the moment of death, even with ten recitations, the Buddha will surely come to welcome one.

How true it is that he said the Pure Land is very easy to reach! After the official agreed with these words, he continued by saying: "Now that the carving of the printing blocks has been completed..."
May this biography endure for a long time, so that those who read it may be moved to feel a sense of resonance.

If they further exhort one another and cultivate mindfulness to the utmost degree—making their own homes a Pure Land and themselves Amitābha—then the Master’s vow will be fulfilled, and his mission will be complete. (End)
Thus, I have respectfully written this to assist in the wide propagation of the Great Repentance. This is also one way to ensure longevity, merit, and the prosperity of the state.
Written on the first day of the second month of the Canglong Bingchen year by Park [Mian] To-bu, the hermit of Yakan.
Colophon to the *Mida Daichō Zange Hō* (The Method of Repentance for the Amitābha Sanctuary).
On the [blank] day of the ninth month of autumn in the fourth year of the Chenghua era, the Great Sovereign suddenly abandoned his ministers. I...
His Highness’s grief and longing are boundless. He has produced a printed copy of the *Mida Chankan Hō* (Amitābha Repentance Ritual) and recited it by the side of the bier.
Your servant has heard the Great Hero say:
"In the West lies the Land of Immeasurable Life, named Sukhāvatī; with a single thought of faith, one shall immediately [attain rebirth]."
One attains rebirth and experiences all manner of bliss. This method of repentance subdues the majestic spiritual power of the Buddhas and expiates the karmic obstacles of many lifetimes.
It points directly to the path of rebirth and is truly a staircase for attaining Buddhahood.
It is what is called "the single secret for rebirth in the Western Pure Land" and "the supreme Bodhi entrusted into both hands."
Indeed, our Great King has long planted the roots of virtue and thoroughly penetrated the True Vehicle.

His veneration of the Triple Gem and his grand proclamation of the profound transformation are attested by all the Buddhas and devas of the ten directions; how could it be merely a matter of a single moment of faithful resolve?
They transcend to the pure realm and suddenly realize the fruit of Buddhahood; of this there is no doubt.

Pushing this to its ultimate limit, the benefits are impartially bestowed throughout the worlds of the ten directions, such that all together achieve the unsurpassed, perfect fruition. Only then does it cease. Alas!
How difficult is it to measure!
Respectfully inscribed by His Majesty’s Subject, Li Ke-dun, Grand Councilor of the Ministry of Rites, of the Rank of Tongzheng Dafu.
